title: Learning by trying: tests, bandits and reinforcement learning
hook: A/B tests, bandits, contextual bandits, full reinforcement learning, or plain optimization.
inPlainWords: When an AI's choice changes what happens next, it can learn from the results. The methods range from simple experiments to full reinforcement learning. Use the lightest one that fits.

useCase.title: Which discount banner should the home page show?
useCase.story: Three banners: 10% off, free shipping, and a bundle deal. Every visitor sees one, and you learn from what they buy. Tastes shift by season.

approaches.name: Rules or gut feeling
approaches.example: Marketing says free shipping always wins.

approaches.name: A/B test
approaches.what: Show each version to a fixed share of visitors, then compare.
approaches.greatWhen: One clear decision and enough traffic, when you want a clean answer.
approaches.avoidWhen: Many options or changing tastes. It wastes traffic on losers.

approaches.name: Bandit
approaches.what: Send more visitors to whichever banner is winning, while still testing the others.
approaches.greatWhen: Many options, when you want to earn while you learn.
approaches.avoidWhen: Results show up only weeks later.
approaches.example: After a day, the best banner gets 70% of visitors.

approaches.name: Contextual bandit
approaches.what: Choose using clues about the visitor, like device and past orders.
approaches.avoidWhen: There is little data per group.
approaches.example: Bundle deals for repeat buyers, free shipping for first-time visitors.

approaches.name: Full reinforcement learning
approaches.what: Learn a strategy across a long series of decisions with delayed rewards.
approaches.greatWhen: Sequences like pricing over weeks, robots, or logistics.
approaches.avoidWhen: You have no safe simulator, or feedback is scarce.
approaches.example: Learn when to raise or cut prices across a season.

approaches.name: Optimization solver
approaches.what: Compute the best plan under known constraints. No learning needed.
approaches.greatWhen: Rules and costs are known, like routes and schedules.

challenge.question: Three banners, lots of traffic, and tastes that shift by season. What is the smart fit?

options.why: You have traffic to learn from. Use it.

options.text: One two-week A/B test, then never revisit
options.why: Clean, but it goes stale when tastes shift.

options.text: A bandit that keeps shifting traffic toward winners
options.why: It earns while it learns and notices seasonal change.

options.text: Full reinforcement learning with a custom simulator
options.why: Massive overkill for a three-way choice.

bestCase.title: Use the lightest method that fits the decision
bestCase.example: A bandit sends most visitors to the current best banner and keeps a few percent exploring. When autumn arrives and free shipping stops winning, it notices within days and shifts.

worstCase.title: Overbuilding, or never learning
worstCase.example: The team spends six months building a full reinforcement-learning system with a custom simulator, when a bandit would have worked in a week. Or they pick one banner from opinion and never check that it works.

steps.label: Visitor arrives
steps.goes: A new visitor opens the home page.

steps.label: Choose a banner
steps.goes: Mostly the current best, sometimes another to keep learning.
steps.goesWrong: The banner was chosen by opinion, and nobody ever checks the result.

steps.label: Show it
steps.goes: The banner appears on the page.

steps.label: Watch what happens
steps.goes: Did the visitor click or buy?

steps.label: Repeat
steps.goes: The next visitor gets a smarter choice.

takeaway: When choices shape outcomes, learn from the results. Start with a test or a bandit before reinforcement learning.
